nodes.label: HMAC-authenticated Sequenced Audio Chunks
nodes.rationale: Kiosk streams a live conversation over an open WebSocket, so each chunk carries a sequence number + per-session HMAC to prevent tampering/replay. Integrity, not confidentiality — TLS handles the latter upstream.

nodes.label: Resumable Staged Audit State Machine
nodes.rationale: Transcribe/acoustic/analyze are separate stages that each persist output so a transient Deepgram/LLM failure resumes mid-pipeline instead of re-running everything. Caveat: default retry count is effectively 1 today per the engineering audit.

nodes.label: Enhancement Split into Separate FFmpeg Service
nodes.rationale: AEC/denoise is CPU-heavy and FFmpeg-native; isolating it in its own file-in/file-out HTTP service keeps the ingest service responsive.
nodes.norm_label: enhancement split into separate ffmpeg service

nodes.label: Property Rules Pulled from Platform (not owned here)
nodes.rationale: The audit must reflect per-hotel policy managed by admins in kiotel_web; audio_services reads it over an internal endpoint so there is one source of truth.
nodes.norm_label: property rules pulled from platform (not owned here)

nodes.label: Single-Worker Constraint on Ingest Service
nodes.rationale: Session registry, rate limiter, and audit semaphore are in-process, so the service is pinned to one worker (flock-enforced). Caps horizontal scale until that state moves to Redis; flagged in the audit as the main scaling blocker.

nodes.label: Prompt-as-Code LLM Auditor Rubric
nodes.rationale: The LLM audit rubric (check-in/walk-in/check-out scripts, fraud definition) lives as a large system prompt defining what a good check-in looks like — the semantic core of the service.

nodes.label: Known Risks — leaked Deepgram key, unauthenticated audit endpoint, no encryption at rest, indefinite transcript retention, ~46% dead WIP code

nodes.label: Property-Scoped Multi-Tenancy (customer → customer_properties → everything)
nodes.rationale: One deployment serves many hotel-owner clients; every inventory/booking object hangs off property_id and property-guards verify ownership on every request so staff of property A cannot reach property B by changing the URL.

nodes.label: Advisory-Locked Confirmation Numbers (pg_advisory_xact_lock per property)
nodes.rationale: Booking confirmation numbers must be unique and gap-controlled per hotel under concurrent front-desk activity; the DB function next_confirmation_number() serializes generation.

nodes.label: Tax/Rate Snapshots Frozen onto the Reservation
nodes.rationale: Taxes and nightly rates are frozen onto the reservation at booking time so a later rate/tax change never retroactively alters a historical booking's totals.
nodes.norm_label: tax/rate snapshots frozen onto the reservation

nodes.label: Hand-Built Tape-Chart Calendar (CalendarScreen)
nodes.rationale: Hotel front desks think in a room × date grid with drag-to-move/resize; the booking UX is built around that mental model, gated by per-status edit capabilities.

nodes.label: argon2id + Rotating Refresh Tokens with Reuse-Detection
nodes.rationale: Deliberately stronger auth than the legacy stack; a replayed refresh token revokes all sessions for the principal. Delivered as audience-namespaced httpOnly cookies.
nodes.norm_label: argon2id + rotating refresh tokens with reuse-detection

nodes.label: Reservation Lifecycle — 9-state machine with whitelisted transitions
nodes.rationale: Creation runs in one DB transaction: find-or-create guest → advisory-locked confirmation number → insert reservation + nightly rates + addons + tax snapshots. Every transition is logged and mutates the room's front-office status.
nodes.norm_label: reservation lifecycle — 9-state machine with whitelisted transitions

nodes.label: kiotel-storage DigitalOcean Space — shared bucket, anonymous GetObject policy on image prefixes only
nodes.rationale: Objects uploaded via the S3 API are private by default and the Space's File Listing setting governs listing only, so an explicit bucket policy is required or the CDN returns 403. The Space is shared with other apps and put-bucket-policy replaces the whole policy, so existing statements must be merged in. Guest documents and DB dumps deliberately stay private (presigned URLs).

nodes.label: ClickOnce Publish-Output Repo Layout
nodes.rationale: The repo is a ClickOnce publish output, not a clean source tree: real app source lives under Application Files/core_kiosk/kiosk_Source/, everything else ending in _Source is vendored third-party library source plus ~90 DLLs and multi-GB OCR models. Tooling and graphing must target kiosk_Source/ and docs/ and exclude vendored binaries.

nodes.label: Thin WinForms Shell Hosting WebView2 UI
nodes.rationale: Guest experience is web content served from the platform so UX changes ship without rebuilding the desktop app; WinForms exists only to own the window, lock down the kiosk, marshal WebSocket commands, and bridge native hardware SDKs.
nodes.norm_label: thin winforms shell hosting webview2 ui

nodes.label: Interface + Real + Simulated Device Pattern
nodes.rationale: The standout design decision: every hardware family has a Simulated* implementation swapped in by simulation_mode, so the entire check-in flow runs on a dev machine with no physical hardware and is testable. New work should build on this seam.

nodes.label: Runtime API Keys From Platform Secrets
nodes.rationale: Deepgram/LLM avatar credentials are fetched from the platform's app_secrets at boot (ApiService.GetSecretsAsync) rather than compiled into the binary, so keys can rotate centrally and never ship on a public terminal. One committed-key exception exists per the audit and should be migrated to this pattern.
nodes.norm_label: runtime api keys from platform secrets

nodes.label: Action-less AI Avatar Design
nodes.rationale: The avatar's LLM output is routed only to TTS with no tool/function calling and no path back into processCommand, structurally neutralizing prompt injection as an actuation vector: a guest can at most make it say something off-script, never dispense cash or keys.

nodes.label: Out-of-Process Device Bridge Executables
nodes.rationale: TWRScannerBridge and U10Bridge run as separate executables reached over localhost HTTP to isolate crash-prone native SDKs from the main process; ChildProcessTracker cleans them up on exit.

nodes.label: Embedded Python + Standalone FastAPI Sidecars
nodes.rationale: Vision/ML work is Python-native; embedding CPython via pythonnet keeps OCR/motion in-process while the heavier YOLO11 alert service runs as its own FastAPI process.

nodes.label: frmMainScreen God Form
nodes.rationale: A ~6,900-line single form owning WebView controls, the Socket.IO client, the RELAY dispatcher, Google TTS/Translate, Google Meet, motion streaming, and the AI avatar; documented as a single point of fragility.

nodes.label: Known Engineering Risks (Kiosk)
nodes.rationale: God form fragility, swallow-and-continue global exception handlers with no watchdog, unset WebView2 lockdown flags, dispense commands over an unsigned socket channel, and a committed cloud key in the publish output.

nodes.label: IIDScanner (ID/Passport Reader Abstraction)
nodes.rationale: Multiple implementations (SinosecuLocalScanner, SinosecuSDKScanner, OldScannerBridge, clsIDScanner) exist because deployments use different physical readers with incompatible SDKs; the interface hides that from the command dispatcher.

nodes.label: LicenseStore + HardwareFingerprint
nodes.rationale: DPAPI-encrypted license.dat holds the device secret, bound to a SHA-256 hardware fingerprint of CPU/board/disk serials + MachineGuid so a license cannot be copied between machines.

nodes.label: Legal Document Fill & Sign in WebView
nodes.norm_label: legal document fill & sign in webview

nodes.label: Hub-and-Spoke Topology (kiotel_web as Hub)
nodes.rationale: kiotel_web is the tower everything talks to: kiosks hold device-authenticated Socket.IO connections for RELAY commands and telemetry; audio services, the PMS partner API, and the ML services all route through the platform rather than talking to each other directly.

nodes.label: Two Databases, Two Hotel/Guest Models
nodes.rationale: There is no shared hotel or guest table across the system: the PMS owns the rich multi-tenant model (customers -> customer_properties -> rooms/guests/reservations) while the platform is device/agent/session centric with a free-text hotelname and per-session guest identity (t_session_info, id_scanjobs).

nodes.label: Check-in-Time Name Match Bridge
nodes.rationale: Because no shared guest table exists, the bridge between PMS and platform identity is matching the OCR'd name from the scan pipeline against t_session_info.guest_name populated per session by an agent or the PMS-autofill extension.

nodes.norm_label: handlesubmit (posts submit to webview2 host or backend api)

nodes.label: Person & Dog Detection Pipeline (WS in -> YOLO11n CPU -> SSE out)
nodes.rationale: Camera streams JPEG frames in over WebSocket, YOLO11n detects person/dog on CPU (no GPU needed, i5 8th gen sufficient), and alerts are pushed out via SSE to the dashboard; cooldown was replaced by a presence timeout so the same person does not re-alert.
nodes.norm_label: person & dog detection pipeline (ws in -> yolo11n cpu -> sse out)

nodes.label: Detector Runtime Configuration (settings.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Tunable without touching code; every value overridable via DETECTOR__ env vars. presence_timeout_seconds replaced cooldown_seconds; frame queue drops old frames to stay real-time.
